unsafe_pattern: Applying a recursive chmod (e.g. `execa(.sync)('chmod', ['-R', 'a+rX', dir])`, an equivalent shell string containing `chmod -R`, or `fs.chmodSync`/`fs.promises.chmod` walked recursively over a directory tree) to a directory that also holds, or may in the future hold, files intentionally created with a restrictive mode (e.g. 0o600) for sensitive content such as audit logs, tokens, or credentials.
consequence: The recursive chmod silently widens permissions on every file under the target directory, including files deliberately locked down to owner-only access. Sensitive audit/token/log payloads become world- or group-readable, an information-disclosure defect that is easy to reintroduce because the recursive call looks like ordinary cleanup/log-permission-repair code.
mechanical_correction: Restrict the chmod to the specific top-level directory and its direct (non-recursive) files only, or explicitly enumerate/exclude known-sensitive subpaths before any recursive step. When a file must stay private, create it with the restrictive mode via `fs.openSync(path, flags, 0o600)` + `fs.fchmodSync` (or equivalent) rather than relying on a later broad chmod pass to skip it.

evidence.title: Preserve redacted upstream non-2xx payloads and correlation metadata in API proxy audit logs
evidence.detail: Changed containers/api-proxy/token-persistence.js audit log file mode from 0o644 to 0o600 and added explicit fs.openSync+fchmodSync to avoid a transient world-readable window; added a test asserting the file mode stays 0o600.

evidence.title: fix: preserve API proxy log cleanup permissions
evidence.detail: Removed recursive chmod widening (`chmodRuntimeDir`) for the API-proxy logs directory and removed proxyLogsDir from the recursive `fixArtifactPermissionsForRootless` fix-up list, specifically to stop `chmod -R a+rX` from exposing the 0600 token-tracker-audit.jsonl file that lives in the same directory tree.

Unresolved copilot-pull-request-reviewer comment noting the #8562 fix was incomplete: src/container-stop.ts still runs `chmod -R a+rX /var/log/squid` (via fixSquidLogPermissions), which shares the same host directory as the 0600 token-tracker-audit.jsonl file, so the file is world-readable again before the direct-files-only cleanup in artifact-preservation.ts runs.

likely_false_positives: Recursive chmod on directories that are guaranteed never to contain restricted-mode files (e.g. purely public build-output directories) is safe; the rule should allow an explicit exclusion/allowlist comment or a narrower non-recursive alternative to suppress.
existing_plugin_coverage: None found in eslint-plugin-security or typescript-eslint recommended configs; this is a repo-specific security pattern not covered by a published rule.
